n1.speaker: Arantxa
n1.text: ¡Hola, Vinícius! Bienvenido a casa. Soy Arantxa, la madre de Unai. ¿Tienes hambre? La cena es a las nueve y media.
n1.translation: Hi Vinícius! Welcome home. I'm Arantxa, Unai's mom. Hungry? Dinner is at half past nine.

n2.text: Nine and a half. It is 19:00. You have been hungry since the bus passed Burgos.

choices.text: Smile and nod. Nodding is universal.

n3.speaker: Arantxa
n3.text: ¡Ay, qué majo! Toma unas galletas mientras tanto. Tu habitación está arriba, a la izquierda.
n3.translation: Oh, how sweet! Have some biscuits meanwhile. Your room is upstairs, on the left.

n3b.speaker: Arantxa
n3b.text: Vale, vale. Tu habitación está arriba, a la izquierda. ¡A las nueve y media!
n3b.translation: Okay, okay. Your room is upstairs, on the left. Half past nine!

effects.log: Met Arantxa. Dinner is at 21:30. Twenty-one thirty.

n1.speaker: Arantxa
n1.text: Todavía no. A las nueve y media. ¡Paciencia, que la menestra no se hace sola!
n1.translation: Not yet. Half past nine. Patience, the menestra doesn't cook itself!

n1.speaker: Arantxa
n1.text: ¡A cenar! He hecho menestra, mi plato estrella. Guisantes, alcachofas, espárragos, judías verdes...
n1.translation: Dinner! I made menestra, my star dish. Peas, artichokes, asparagus, green beans...

n2.text: Peas. A whole stew built around peas. Under the table, Txuri looks up at you with the eyes of a professional.

choices.text: Eat the peas. All of them. For Portugal.
Slip the peas to Txuri, one spoon at a time.

eat.text: You chew. You swallow. You do not make a face. Somewhere, a diplomat is proud.

effects.log: Ate a plate of menestra. Every pea.

esq.speaker: Arantxa
esq.translation: Exquisite?! Iñaki, he said it's exquisite!

esq2.text: In Portuguese, 'esquisito' means weird. In Spanish, 'exquisito' means delicious. You just paid the biggest compliment of your life by accident. Keep it.

effects.log: Told Arantxa the menestra was 'esquisito'. She was thrilled. (Portuguese: weird. Spanish: delicious.)

dog.text: Txuri accepts the peas in silence. Then a second spoon. Then Nahia's voice:

dog2.speaker: Nahia
dog2.translation: Mom! The dog is eating peas!

dog3.speaker: Arantxa
dog3.text: ¡Txuri! ... Vinícius, ¿no te gustan los guisantes? ¡Haberlo dicho, hombre!
dog3.translation: Txuri! ... Vinícius, you don't like peas? You should have said!

choices.text: "Sorry... I really, really don't like peas."

honest.speaker: Arantxa
honest.text: Pues tortilla y ya está. Aquí no se pasa hambre.
honest.translation: Then tortilla, and that's that. Nobody goes hungry in this house.

effects.log: Fed the peas to Txuri. Got caught. Got tortilla.

blame.speaker: Arantxa
blame.text: Ya. Y yo soy la reina de Navarra. Anda, tortilla.
blame.translation: Sure. And I'm the queen of Navarre. Come on, tortilla.

effects.log: Fed the peas to Txuri and blamed the dog. Got tortilla anyway.

end.speaker: Arantxa
end.text: Mañana hay almuerzo a las once en el instituto. Unai te enseña. ¡Buenas noches!
end.translation: Tomorrow there's almuerzo at eleven at school. Unai will show you. Good night!

n1.speaker: Arantxa
n1.text: ¿Cansado? Tu cama está arriba. Mañana, a las siete. ¡Egun on!
n1.translation: Tired? Your bed is upstairs. Tomorrow, seven o'clock. Good morning!

n1.speaker: Arantxa
n1.text: ¡Egun on! Desayuna algo. Y a las once, almuerzo, que aquí la comida es a las dos.
n1.translation: Morning! Eat something. And almuerzo at eleven, because lunch here is at two.

effects.log: Breakfast at Unai's. Lunch here is at 14:00, which feels like a prank.

n1.speaker: Arantxa
n1.text: ¡A cenar! Hoy, tortilla de patatas. Sin guisantes.
n1.translation: Dinner! Today, potato omelette. No peas.

effects.log: Dinner at 21:30. Getting used to it. Almost.

n1.speaker: Arantxa
n1.text: ¿Todo bien? La cena a las nueve y media. No lo olvides.
n1.translation: All good? Dinner at half past nine. Don't forget.

n2.text: That's it. That's the greeting. Then he looks back at his phone.

u2.speaker: Unai
u2.text: Sí. Es euskera. Aquí hablamos castellano y euskera. Jajaja.
u2.translation: Yes. It's Basque. Here we speak Spanish and Basque. Hahaha.

effects.log: Met Unai. He says 'jajaja' out loud, like in the chat.

n1.speaker: Unai
n1.text: Jajaja. ¿Has visto la carta debajo de la almohada? ...Yo no he sido.
n1.translation: Hahaha. Did you see the card under the pillow? ...It wasn't me.

n2.speaker: Unai
n2.text: No sé. En serio. Pero el año pasado a mi prima le pasó lo mismo en Gaia.
n2.translation: I don't know. Seriously. But last year the same thing happened to my cousin in Gaia.

effects.log: Unai swears he didn't plant the tarot card. His cousin got one in Gaia last year.

n2.speaker: Unai
n2.text: Mañana pelota vasca. Tú, baloncesto. Trato. Jajaja.
n2.translation: Tomorrow Basque pelota. You, basketball. Deal. Hahaha.

n1.speaker: Nahia
n1.text: ¿Juegas a Roblox? Tengo tres mundos. En uno hay un pollo gigante.
n1.translation: Do you play Roblox? I have three worlds. One has a giant chicken.

yes.speaker: Nahia
yes.text: ¡Vale! Después de cenar. El pollo se llama Pollo.
yes.translation: Okay! After dinner. The chicken is called Chicken.

effects.log: Promised Nahia to see her Roblox chicken. It is called Chicken.

later.speaker: Nahia
later.translation: Fine. The chicken will wait for you.

n1.speaker: Iñaki
n1.text: ¿Linkin Park? ¿En serio? Yo tenía tu edad cuando salió Hybrid Theory.
n1.translation: Linkin Park? Seriously? I was your age when Hybrid Theory came out.

choices.text: "In the End is the best one."

best.speaker: Iñaki
best.text: Discutible. Pero bien. Mañana en el coche, la discográfica entera.
best.translation: Debatable. But fine. Tomorrow in the car, the whole discography.

effects.log: Argued with Iñaki about the best Linkin Park song. He was your age in 2000.

which.speaker: Iñaki
which.text: Todas. Mañana en el coche te las pongo.
which.translation: All of them. Tomorrow in the car I'll play them for you.

effects.log: Iñaki, architect and Linkin Park fan, promised a car-ride playlist.

n1.speaker: Iñaki
n1.text: Esta casa está orientada al sur. Bioclimática. Te lo explico el jueves, con la ecociudad.
n1.translation: This house faces south. Bioclimatic. I'll explain on Thursday, with the eco-city.

n1.speaker: Aitona Joxemari
n1.text: ¿Ajedrez? Apertura española. Ruy López, 1561. La escribió contra un portugués, Damiano. Mañana, la revancha.
n1.translation: Chess? The Spanish Opening. Ruy López, 1561. He wrote it against a Portuguese, Damiano. Tomorrow, the rematch.

effects.log: Aitona Joxemari challenged you to a chess rematch 450 years in the making.

word.speaker: Aitona Joxemari
word.text: Aitona, sí. Abuelo. Y amona, abuela. Mañana, ajedrez.
word.translation: Aitona, yes. Grandfather. And amona, grandmother. Tomorrow, chess.

effects.log: Aitona Joxemari challenged you to a chess rematch. Learned what 'aitona' means.

n1.text: Txuri wags his whole body. 'Txuri' means 'white' in Basque. Txuri is, in fact, very white.
